ledger.note: 24: Lu Fang rises in the north. The Lu Fang disambiguation page dates him 'fl. 24-41'; the Guangwu page dates no rise and has him controlling 'the modern central and western Inner Mongolia region' with the Xiongnu chanyu Yu's support. PAGE SILENT on the year of his rise and on his title of emperor.

ledger.note: 42: Lu Fang flees. He 'eventually fled to Xiongnu in AD 42' after submitting and being made Prince of Dai (no date); the disambiguation page's 'fl. 24-41' differs by a year. [Reviewer ea-02-x, 2026-10-19: the page says Lu Fang fled to the Xiongnu after being made Prince of Dai; it does not say his land passed to the Xiongnu; confidence lowered from 3 to 2] [fx-02, 2026-11-01: counterpart xiongnu changed to nobody. The Emperor Guangwu page (re-opened) says only that Lu Fang 'eventually fled to Xiongnu in AD 42' after submitting and being made Prince of Dai, and nothing about who held the land; with xiongnu as the counterpart the compiler gave the Ordos and Hetao to the Xiongnu in 43-51, over the Han keyframes that draw them, which no page supports.]

notes: Lu Fang, Inner Mongolia under Xiongnu patronage, 24-42. 2 pages opened (Emperor Guangwu of Han; the Lu Fang disambiguation page, which lists 'Lu Fang (warlord)' as a red link). No Cliopatria row, no article. Unsettled: everything but the control of central and western Inner Mongolia and the flight in 42: the rise year (24 is the disambiguation page's 'fl.'), the title, the capital, his stay as Prince of Dai, the Xiongnu tie (the page says the chanyu Yu supported him: a client relation to record in the xiongnu dossier). Counterparts: xin-dynasty, xiongnu exist.
